newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentine wheat sales reach 4.40 mln tns mid-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat sales reach 4.40 mln tns mid-Nov.

text.p: Argentine sales of wheat reached around 4.40 million tonnes by mid-November, according to figures distributed by officials from the Argentine Agricultural Secretariat at a wheat conference in Rio de Janeiro.
The biggest buyer so far is Brazil which has bought 1.3 million, with the second largest Iran at 600,000 tonnes.
Argentina will produce at least 14 million to 14.5 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97, Argentine Agricultural Secretary Felipe Sola told reporters.
It may also reach the 15 million tonne mark, with the most recent crop report from the Secretariat estimating a harvest of 14.9 million tonnes.
"We are in some doubt about what will be the final figure. Last year we were estimating around 8.6 million tonnes at this time and it ended up one million tonnes more," Sola said.
Exports will account for around 10 million tonnes, with Brazil possibly buying up to six million tonnes, Sola said.
"It may be five million, it may be 5.5, it may be six million tonnes. We want to sell as much as we can," Sola said.
In 1995, Brazil accounted for 4.38 million tonnes of total exports of 6.78 million tonnes, according to secretariat figures.

Apart from an increase in planted area, the rise in output has come from better productivity. Use of fertilizers has risen sharply, with 60 to 70 percent of planted area of 6.8 million hectares fertilised against only 40 to 50 percent last year.
The recent sharp fall in international wheat prices moreover is not likely to deter farmers from planting wheat next year, with production costs around $60 a tonne, Sola said.
"I don't think the 1997/98 crop will fall much," he said.
Sales of new crop by 14/11/1996 by country in tonnes follow.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
